content.user_title: Craft Clear LinkedIn Posts and Stronger Hooks
content.value_statement: LinkedIn drafts often lack clear openings, concrete evidence, and readable structure. This skill provides hook variants, concise post formatting, and focused founder-voice critique.
actual_capabilities: Generate five hook variants using contrarian, specific evidence, confession, pattern observation, and question reframe archetypes.
Recommend one primary hook with a short explanation.
Reformat finished posts with a one-sentence opener, separate body lines, evidence bullets, and a direct closing sentence.
Apply a 200-word limit, a three-hashtag limit, and restrictions against emoji blocks and engagement bait.
Critique hook strength, evidence, founder voice, formatting, and writing anti-patterns; rewrite the weakest line.
Generate three stronger hook candidates for a topic and recommend the strongest.
limitations: Designed as a sub-skill loaded by founder-brand, with direct user invocation disabled in its metadata.
References a companion framework and voice rubric that are not included in the supplied file.
Does not publish posts, retrieve LinkedIn analytics, verify claims, or guarantee audience engagement.
Critique scores are subjective editorial assessments and depend on the supplied draft and available voice guidance.

use_cases.title: Share a Founder Lesson
use_cases.description: Turn a supplied business lesson into hook options and a concise LinkedIn post supported by concrete evidence.

use_cases.title: Improve Client Drafts
use_cases.description: Identify weak openings, vague evidence, and engagement bait before rewriting the weakest line.

use_cases.title: Present Professional Results
use_cases.description: Format a finished project reflection into short body lines, evidence bullets, and a direct closing sentence.

prompt_templates.title: Improve a Topic Hook
prompt_templates.prompt: Give me three stronger LinkedIn hooks for [topic]. Use different archetypes and recommend the strongest.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: improve an opening before drafting.

prompt_templates.title: Explore Five Hook Styles
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate five hook variants for [topic], one per archetype. Use only these facts: [facts]. Recommend a primary hook with a rationale.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: compare alternative openings using supplied evidence.

prompt_templates.title: Format a Finished Post
prompt_templates.prompt: Reformat this LinkedIn draft for quick reading: [draft]. Preserve the facts and voice. Use evidence bullets, at most 200 words, and three hashtags.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare an existing draft for manual publication.

prompt_templates.title: Critique and Revise
prompt_templates.prompt: Critique this draft against the available founder voice rubric: [draft]. Report dimension scores, anti-patterns, the weakest-line rewrite, and an editorial verdict. Explain each score.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: review a draft with the companion framework available.

output_examples.input: Suggest stronger hooks about onboarding. Supplied fact: simplifying a checklist reduced setup time from six days to four.
output: Contrarian: Our onboarding improvement came from a simpler checklist, not another training session.
Specific evidence: Setup time fell from six days to four after we simplified the onboarding checklist.
Question reframe: Instead of asking what to add to onboarding, ask which steps people actually need.
Recommended: Use the specific evidence hook because the measured result makes the improvement concrete.

output_examples.input: Format this result as a LinkedIn post: a consultant replaced three status meetings with a shared update and saved two hours weekly.
output_examples.output:
Replacing three status meetings saved our team two hours each week.

We moved routine updates into one shared document.

The change was simple:
- Three status meetings removed.
- One shared update introduced.
- Two hours saved each week.

Keep the conversation for decisions that need it.

#Teamwork #Productivity

output_examples.input: Critique this opening: Leadership is everything. Agree? No supporting evidence or voice rubric is supplied.
output_examples.output:
Weakest line: Leadership is everything.

Rewrite: Name the leadership decision and its observed result before writing the opening.

Rationale: The original claim is broad and unsupported.

Anti-pattern: The closing question requests agreement instead of adding substance.

Verdict: Start over with a concrete example.

best_practices: Provide verified facts, measurements, and examples before requesting evidence-based hooks.
Supply the companion voice rubric when requesting a detailed founder-voice critique.
Review factual accuracy, tone, word count, and hashtags before manually publishing.
anti_patterns: Inventing metrics or personal experiences to make a hook more persuasive.
Adding engagement bait, emoji blocks, or more than three hashtags.
Treating subjective critique scores as objective predictions of audience engagement.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create LinkedIn hook variants, format finished posts, and critique drafts for voice, evidence, and writing anti-patterns.

faq.question: Which hook styles are included?
faq.answer: The five styles are contrarian, specific evidence, confession, pattern observation, and question reframe.

faq.question: Does it publish posts to LinkedIn?
faq.answer: No. The supplied instructions provide writing and critique templates, not account access or publishing automation.

faq.question: Can I invoke it directly?
faq.answer: Its metadata disables direct user invocation. The source describes activation through the parent founder-brand skill.

faq.question: What formatting limits does it specify?
faq.answer: Posts have at most 200 words and three hashtags. The format uses short body lines, evidence bullets, and no emoji blocks.

faq.question: How should I interpret critique scores?
faq.answer: Use them as editorial guidance, not engagement predictions. The five dimensions total 100 points, and the complete voice rubric is external.
